Class Anchor

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.Anchor
public final class Anchor extends Object
A rectangle a library names and supplies per screen, for panels to be placed around with an AnchorPanelAdapter: a slot group's box (SlotKit), the pause menu's button column, the title screen's buttons. MenuKit knows nothing about what the rectangle is; it asks box for it every frame on every open screen. 
public static final Anchor PAUSE_BUTTONS = Anchor.of(
        Identifier.fromNamespaceAndPath("mymod", "pause_buttons"),
        screen -> screen instanceof PauseScreen ? buttonColumn(screen) : null);

The box

Called once per frame per open screen, so it should be a lookup, not a search. It returns the rectangle in screen coordinates, or null when the anchor is not on that screen right now (the wrong screen, or the thing it names is hidden): its panels then take no place and claim nothing. It may be asked about any screen, a container screen or not.

One anchor per id

An id names one rectangle. Declare each Anchor once, keep it, and pass it to every adapter that places against it: panels on one anchor share one host and stack in its regions. A second Anchor.of with an id already declared throws. Anchors are declarations: they freeze with MenuKit's others at client start.
